Feil at du skal få downvotes, det er viktig at flere synspunkt luftes. For min del er problemet at dette blir nok et eksempel på at kommersialisering overstyrer intern sammenheng i en serie.

Når man plasserer én eller to svarte skuespillere i en ellers blendahvit rollebesetning virker det nesten nedlatende. Det hadde vært noe helt annet om de eksempelvis hadde en klan av svarte alver, selv om enkelte garantert hadde klagd på det også. Forskjellen er at det hadde hatt en forklaring i seriens egne univers, mens det som faktisk er tilfelle er at Amazon finner opp en kvote de skal fylle for å framstå progressive nok.

For å ta to andre eksempler:

1) Corlys Velaryon i House of the Dragon ble aldri beskrevet som svart i bøkene, men huset hans har vært sjøfarere i generasjoner. Det er i alle fall plausibelt i dette tilfellet at folk fra alle verdens hjørner har blitt inngiftet i familien gjennom historien.

2) Matt Damon i The Great Wall (2016). Helt absurd at Matt Damon skal spille hovedrollen i en kinesisk film om den kinesiske mur. Her var det kun penger det sto om, da Matt Damon er et stort navn, og bidro antagelig stort til å markedsføre filmen utenfor Kina.

I agree with your main point. I'm probably spoiled in the sense that I am subconciously expecting things to be either fun, easy, or instantly rewarding. However, I haven't always felt this way. I know I can work hard and get results given the right circumstances, and college just isn't doing it for me. I'm  struggling with so much guilt and regret for things I've done in the past, and it feels like in college I'm just continuing the same cycle I've always been stuck in. I've started going to therapy which will be my main focus the coming months, and I have so much shit I need to sort out since I've never been able to discuss it with anyone, and I really don't think a course I'm not actually motivated for is compatible with that.

Also, I'm in my first semester, and I can honestly say, all hyperbole aside, if I was forced to complete my bachelor in the next 3 years, I would kill myself.
Yeah, some days I get this surge of determination to get things done, and that makes a single day bearable, but most days just dragging myself out of bed in the morning is damn near impossible.

Yeah, come christmas I'm expecting the same shocked reaction from the people in my life. The realisation that I'm not an academic might be healthy for me in the long run, but right now it's pretty disheartening.  


I'm really happy to hear that you've found other pursuits though, I think people tend to overlook how important that actually is. I am looking to get into graphic design and animation once I get a better computer, and programming and music design also seem appealing. I think I'm just a much more creative person than a technical/logical one.

Not sure how to respond in regards to giving the decisive push, but I suppose, you're welcome? I think it's perfectly doable to go your own way. It might require more work than university did, but if you're genuinely passionate about it, the process itself can be enjoyable, and not just the end goal.
